record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Existence of SIC-POVMs in all dimensions
record.original_question: For every Hilbert-space dimension d, does there exist a symmetric informationally complete POVM: a set of d squared normalized vectors forming equiangular lines, whose associated rank-one projection operators sum to a multiple of the identity and are linearly independent so that every quantum state can be reconstructed from the resulting measurement statistics?

evidence.quote: A set of d2 normed vectors {|φii}i in a Hilbert space of dimension d constitutes a set of equiangular lines if their mutual inner products |hφi|φj i|2 are independent of the choice of i 6= j.

A POVM that arises in this way is called symmetric informationally complete, or a SIC-POVM for short.
The most general form of the problem is: decide if SIC-POVMs exists in any dimension d.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H} = \mathbb{C}^d$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d \ge 2$. A symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measure (SIC-POVM) on $\mathcal{H}$ is a collection of $d^2$ unit vectors $\{|\varphi_i\rangle\}_{i=1}^{d^2} \subset \mathcal{H}$ such that:

(i) (Equiangularity) There exists a constant $c$ with
$$|\langle \varphi_i \mid \varphi_j \rangle|^2 = c \quad \text{for all } i \ne j,$$
and one easily checks that $c$ must equal $\tfrac{1}{d+1}$.

(ii) (Resolution of the identity) The associated rank-one projectors $\Pi_i = |\varphi_i\rangle\langle \varphi_i|$ satisfy
$$\sum_{i=1}^{d^2} \Pi_i = d\, I,$$
so that $\{\tfrac{1}{d}\Pi_i\}_{i=1}^{d^2}$ is a POVM.

(iii) (Informational completeness) The operators $\{\Pi_i\}_{i=1}^{d^2}$ are linearly independent in the real vector space of Hermitian operators on $\mathcal{H}$, hence form a basis, and every density operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal{H}$ is uniquely determined by the probabilities $\mathrm{tr}(\rho \Pi_i)/d$.

Question: Does a SIC-POVM exist for every finite dimension $d \ge 2$?
artifact.status_search_result: The general existence of SIC-POVMs in all finite dimensions (Zauner's conjecture) remains an open problem as of 2025. Exact and/or numerical solutions are known in many specific dimensions (all $d \le 151$ and additional sporadic cases such as $d = 23$ and various dimensions reachable by Stark-unit constructions), and recent algebraic number theory approaches have produced new exact fiducials, but no proof of existence in arbitrary dimension is known.

status_evidence.title: SIC POVMs and Zauner's Conjecture – Open Quantum Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Zauner's conjecture on the existence of SIC-POVMs in all finite dimensions is listed as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of SIC-POVMs in all dimensions is still listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: SIC-POVM - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is commonly believed that SIC-POVMs exist in all dimensions; however, the general proof of their existence is still an open problem.

status_evidence.title: SIC-POVMs from Stark Units: Dimensions n^2+3=4p
status_evidence.snippet: New exact SIC fiducials constructed via Stark units in specific families of dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial constructions exist in further specific dimensions but not all.
